answer_verbatim:
For Kansas City, I’d start by booking **2–4 free orthodontic consultations** rather than choosing solely from reviews or an “Invisalign Diamond” badge. Here’s a practical call list of established KC-area orthodontic practices to compare:

| Practice to call | Best fit / why call |
|---|---|
| **Fry Orthodontic Specialists** — multiple KC-metro offices on both the Kansas and Missouri sides | A large, orthodontist-focused local group with convenient locations and broad experience in both braces and Invisalign/clear aligners. Good first call if convenience, lots of appointment options, and financing flexibility matter. Ask which orthodontist would personally oversee your treatment. |
| **Bulleigh Orthodontics** — Johnson County / Overland Park–Olathe area | Worth a consultation if you’re on the Kansas side and want a more local-practice feel. They are focused on orthodontics rather than general dentistry and offer both traditional braces and clear-aligner options. |
| **Kanning Orthodontics** — Johnson County / Lenexa–Overland Park area | Another strong consultation option for patients in Johnson County. Compare their proposed treatment plan and total fee against Fry and Bulleigh, especially if you have crowding, bite issues, or a prior orthodontic relapse. |
| **Trimmell Anders & White Orthodontics** — Kansas City North / Northland area | A sensible call for Northland residents who prefer an orthodontic specialty practice close to home. Ask specifically whether your case is better treated with Invisalign, braces, or a hybrid approach. |
| **McClain Orthodontics** — Missouri-side / Kansas City–Liberty area | Particularly worth considering if you live in the Northland or Missouri side and want a dedicated orthodontic office rather than receiving aligners through a general dentist. |
| **Westrock Orthodontics** — multiple metro-area locations | Useful as a price and convenience comparison because of its broad footprint and scheduling availability. Make sure to ask who your treating orthodontist is and how often you will actually see that doctor rather than only a clinical team member. |

### My short list by area

- **Overland Park, Olathe, Lenexa, Shawnee:** Call **Bulleigh, Kanning, and Fry**.  
- **Kansas City North, Liberty, Parkville:** Call **Trimmell Anders & White, McClain, and Fry**.  
- **Kansas City, Lee’s Summit, Independence, Missouri side:** Call **Fry, McClain, and Westrock**; add a nearby independent orthodontic specialty office for comparison.  

### Why these are better starting points than an Invisalign ad
Look for an **orthodontist**—a dentist with specialty orthodontic training—not just a general dentist who sells clear aligners. That matters most if you have any of the following:

- a significant overbite, underbite, crossbite, or open bite  
- jaw pain or teeth that do not meet well  
- crowding that may require extra space or tooth movement beyond simple alignment  
- a prior braces/Invisalign relapse  
- a teen who may still be growing  

Invisalign can be excellent, including for many complex cases, but braces may be more predictable or efficient for certain bite corrections. A good orthodontist should explain *why* they recommend one over the other—not simply steer every patient toward the product they sell most.

### What to ask on every call
Use the same questions so you can compare apples to apples:

1. **Will a board-certified orthodontist diagnose and oversee my case?**  
   Board certification through the **American Board of Orthodontics** is a useful extra credential, though not the only marker of quality.

2. **Do you recommend braces, Invisalign, or either—and why for my bite?**

3. **What is the all-in price?**  
   Ask whether it includes records/scans, attachments, retainers, broken brackets, refinement aligners, emergency visits, and post-treatment follow-up.

4. **How long is the expected treatment?**  
   Also ask what could make it longer.

5. **How often will I see the orthodontist personally?**

6. **What happens if I finish Invisalign and still need refinements?**  
   This is especially important; some quotes include refinements and some do not.

7. **What retainers are included, and what is the replacement cost?**  
   Retention is not optional—teeth can shift after either braces or aligners.

### A good decision rule
Choose the office where you get:

- a clear explanation of your bite and treatment choices,
- a written all-inclusive quote,
- realistic—not overly fast—timing,
- confidence in the orthodontist who will actually manage the case,
- and an office location/schedule you can stick with.

For most people, I would schedule **Fry plus one independent Johnson County or Missouri-side practice near you**, then compare both treatment plans and the total fee.
